title: Keys committed to code (the TiDB Cloud lesson)
summary: PingCAP, the company behind TiDB Cloud, confirmed that stolen service-account credentials gave an attacker access to its internal systems from 9 September to 7 October. The attackers allege they used cloud keys committed to the company's own repositories. Keys in code are copied wherever the code goes.
fix: If a finding is a real key: revoke or rotate it at the provider first (deleting it from the code doesn't un-leak it; it stays in git history and every clone), then remove it and load it from a secret manager or the environment. For the whole history, run a dedicated scanner such as gitleaks or trufflehog.
